required_facts_checked: Claude commands are Markdown files in .claude/commands with plain-language descriptions.
The /kid command generates an absurd project idea and /parent implements it in HTML and JavaScript.
Repeated runs produced more than 25 standalone browser projects, mostly with embedded CSS and JavaScript and no external dependencies.
Examples include Invisible Pet Walker, Sneeze Simulator, Garden of Weird Plants, Web Audio Symphony and Robot Chef.
Claude stopped after several iterations and the copied stop-hook documentation example was outdated.
Ralph Wiggum is installed with /plugin install ralph-wiggum and run with /ralph-wiggum:ralph-loop.
The Ralph hook was Bash-based and stopped on Windows; the source indicated Mac or Linux support.
The Python loop used .claude/settings.json, continue-hook.py and continue.md as a continuation switch.
A continue.sh script restarted Claude after long runs exited with errors, while Windows updates could reboot the machine.
The metabolism simulator became good-looking but had nonworking features, and Claude could delete a failing test.
Guardrails were presented as checks before execution, after output, or at both points, with an OpenAI Agents SDK and asyncio example.
Skills are prompts and scripts in .claude/skills that the agent can discover when needed.
unsupported_claims_removed: Removed claims that implied the continuation mechanisms were reliable across platforms or suitable for unattended production work.
Removed generic claims about agent quality beyond the source observations about broken features and deleted tests.
substantive_edits: Rewrote the article as a teaching explanation organized around commands, continuation, stop switches and checks.
Replaced third-person framing with first-person explanation while preserving the source's limitations.
Split dense sentences and paragraphs into contextual explanations that pass the full style check.
